prompts.prompt: These IAM, KMS, bucket and CloudTrail configs in policies/ go to production Friday for the orders service. Validate them and write security-validation-report.md for the security lead. Do not modify anything in policies/. Do not ask me questions; if something is unclear, make a reasonable assumption and state it in the file.
prompts.why_discriminating: The skill fixes the severity calls (its quality gate makes missing ExternalId, kms:* to a non-admin principal and public bucket access CRITICAL), validates only concrete documents, distinguishes standard patterns from gaps, and scores IAM, encryption, audit logging and compliance into a weighted posture score. Without it, models mis-rank or flag the standard AccountRoot key statement.

floor_checks.text: Report exists and policies/ is unchanged
floor_checks.check: test -f security-validation-report.md && cat policies/cloudtrail.json policies/kms-key-config.json policies/kms-key-policy.json policies/lambda-role-policy.json policies/reports-bucket-policy.json policies/vendor-trust-policy.json | sha256sum | grep -q c5e6f9596db497edc40b7b4219e6572fbda7983d810d0c4192c9f7e1ecf15b94

rubric.criterion: All planted defects found with impact (KEY: s3:* on *; vendor trust without sts:ExternalId; kms:* to orders-app; public read on reports bucket and no aws:SecureTransport; CloudTrail single-region, no global events, no log file validation, no KMS, 30-day retention; key rotation off)
rubric.pass: All six policy files have their defects named with a concrete attack or audit impact

rubric.criterion: Severities follow the skill's quality gate
rubric.pass: s3:* on *, missing ExternalId, kms:* to orders-app and the public bucket are all CRITICAL; rotation and trail gaps High/Medium
rubric.partial: One of the four gate items under-rated
rubric.fail: Two or more gate items rated below CRITICAL, or everything CRITICAL

rubric.criterion: The AccountRoot key statement is not flagged as a vulnerability
rubric.pass: Recognised as the standard key-admin delegation to IAM (may suggest a separate admin role as an improvement)
rubric.partial: Flagged as a medium/low concern without explanation

rubric.pass: IAM, encryption, audit logging and compliance scores out of 100 with the deductions visible, and an overall posture score using the 0.30/0.25/0.25/0.20 weights
rubric.partial: Scores present but no visible derivation or different weights

rubric.pass: Each CRITICAL shows current vs corrected policy JSON (e.g. s3:PutObject/GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-orders-uploads/*, sts:ExternalId condition, kms:Encrypt/Decrypt/GenerateDataKey* for orders-app, Deny without aws:SecureTransport)
rubric.partial: Fixes described in prose without JSON or with one wrong fix

prompts.prompt: Fix the problems in policies/. Write corrected copies with the same file names to policies-fixed/ and keep policies/ as is. Keep the functionality each policy grants: the Lambda uploads to and reads from s3://acme-orders-uploads, the vendor in account 444455556666 reads reports, the app encrypts and decrypts with the key. Add FIXES.md explaining each change. Do not ask me questions; if something is unclear, make a reasonable assumption and state it in the file.
prompts.why_discriminating: The skill's least-privilege rules and quality gate tell the fixer exactly what must change, but the prompt also requires keeping access. Strong fixes tighten without breaking: scoped S3 actions, ExternalId, a non-admin KMS action list while keeping the root statement, TLS-only bucket access for the vendor rather than deleting access.

floor_checks.text: Lambda policy has no wildcard action/resource and vendor trust requires sts:ExternalId
floor_checks.check: python3 -c "import json,sys;d=json.load(open('policies-fixed/lambda-role-policy.json'));L=lambda v:v if isinstance(v,list) else [v];bad=[s for s in d['Statement'] if s.get('Effect')=='Allow' and (any(a=='*' or a.endswith(':*') for a in L(s.get('Action',[]))) or '*' in L(s.get('Resource',[])))];t=json.dumps(json.load(open('policies-fixed/vendor-trust-policy.json')));sys.exit(1 if bad or 'sts:ExternalId' not in t else 0)"

cat policies/cloudtrail.json policies/kms-key-config.json policies/kms-key-policy.json policies/lambda-role-policy.json policies/reports-bucket-policy.json policies/vendor-trust-policy.json | sha256sum | grep -q c5e6f9596db497edc40b7b4219e6572fbda7983d810d0c4192c9f7e1ecf15b94

rubric.pass: Lambda keeps s3:PutObject and s3:GetObject on acme-orders-uploads/* and its DynamoDB read; vendor can still assume the role; orders-app keeps encrypt/decrypt/data-key actions; AccountRoot kept so the key stays manageable
rubric.partial: One required grant dropped or over-narrowed (e.g. missing GetObject)
rubric.fail: Key left unmanageable (root statement removed) or the vendor/app loses access

rubric.criterion: Every gate item and config gap is fixed
rubric.pass: Public Allow removed and replaced with a scoped vendor-role principal, SecureTransport Deny added, CloudTrail multi-region + global events + log file validation + KMS + >= 90-day retention, rotation enabled
rubric.partial: Most fixed, one or two config gaps left

rubric.criterion: No new over-permissive or invented elements
rubric.pass: No new wildcards; placeholders such as the ExternalId value or vendor role ARN are labelled as assumptions in FIXES.md
rubric.partial: One unexplained new grant or an assumed ARN presented as fact
rubric.fail: Introduces new wildcards or broad principals

rubric.criterion: FIXES.md maps each change to a finding and severity
rubric.pass: One entry per change with before/after and the CRITICAL/High label
rubric.partial: Changes listed without severity or rationale

prompts.prompt: Last week's review is reports/security-v1.md. Nobody has changed policies/ since. Re-validate and write security-validation-v2.md for the security lead, showing how things moved since v1. Do not ask me questions; if something is unclear, make a reasonable assumption and state it in the file.
prompts.why_discriminating: The skill's iteration tracking (resolved / remaining / new, posture trend vs the prior score) plus its quality gate means v1's High-rated ExternalId finding should be upgraded to CRITICAL, v1's missed issues reported as new, and the permission-boundary item treated carefully because there is no concrete document behind it.

floor_checks.text: The v2 report exists and references v1's 41/100

rubric.pass: Resolved, remaining and new sections, plus previous 41/100 vs current score and a trend line
rubric.partial: Two of the three groupings or no trend
rubric.fail: A fresh report with no comparison to v1

rubric.criterion: Remaining vs new are classified correctly
rubric.pass: C1, C2, C3 and H1 remain (nothing changed); new: kms:* to orders-app, rotation off, no SecureTransport, single-region trail, no global events, no KMS on trail, 30-day retention
rubric.partial: Mostly right but one v1 issue marked resolved or two new items missing
rubric.fail: Claims progress that did not happen

rubric.criterion: Severity recalibration and v1's H2 are reasoned
rubric.pass: H1 upgraded to CRITICAL with the quality-gate reason; H2 (permission boundary) marked not applicable or withdrawn because no concrete boundary requirement or delegated admin exists
rubric.fail: Both copied from v1 unchanged without comment

rubric.criterion: Does not repeat v1 wholesale or pad
rubric.pass: Text is new analysis; score change explained by the new findings, not a different scale
